title: Travel Protection Plans: Filing a Claim Against the Cancellation Benefit
content:
A journey given up before it begins leaves the traveller holding prepaid outlay the operator has not returned, and a Travel Protection Plans certificate answers that outlay through its cancellation benefit. This page states what the intake of such a claim governs and how the desk puts it in the traveller's hands.

## Applicable situation

The intake arises where the journey a certificate insures has been given up. What is governed is the amount claimed before any limit or deductible is applied.

The amount claimed is worked out only once the certificate carries the declared trip cost the journey insured actually carried. The declared trip cost is the figure the amount claimed is measured on, and it is that figure as the certificate stands at the moment the amount is worked out.

One claim is filed for one incident against one benefit, and where the certificate already carries a claim for that incident against that benefit no further claim is filed. The claim names the benefit it is made against, the insured traveller it belongs to and the day the incident happened.

A claim is filed for an amount on a certificate only after its premium lines carry the re-rating its corrected particulars call for. Until the premium record stands complete in that sense, the certificate is not one on which a claim is filed for an amount.

## Handing the claim to the traveller

The claim is the traveller's own act in their own name, so the tool is theirs rather than the desk's. The representative unlocks the travel protection desk tool `file_cancellation_claim_621a2df1` and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves. One call opens a single claim record on the named certificate for the benefit named, the incident date given and the insured traveller named, recording the amount claimed before any limit or deductible and the evidence supplied. Once the call completes, the claim stands as filed with the insurer against that certificate, and the traveller can see it on their claim statement with the reference the insurer quoted.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy record the claim is made under | Read from the policy record returned by the policy finder |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the traveller profile making the claim | Read from the traveller profile returned by the profile finder |
| `claim_reference` | The claim reference the insurer quoted | Taken from what the traveller reads out and copied character for character, keeping the original wording, digits, spacing and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `claim_type` | The benefit of the plan the claim is made against | Exactly one of the eleven benefits below, and never anything else |
| `incident_date` | The day the insured incident happened | A calendar date YYYY-MM-DD in the traveller's own local calendar, with no time part, never left empty |
| `loss_location_country` | Where the incident happened | An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase, exactly two letters, never left empty |
| `supporting_document_reference` | The reference of the evidence the traveller supplies with the claim | Taken from what the traveller reads out and copied character for character, keeping the original wording, digits, spacing and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `insured_sequence` | Which insured traveller named on the certificate the claim belongs to | A whole number starting at 1 counted in the order the travellers are named, with no decimal part, never left empty |
| `claimed_amount_usd` | The amount being claimed before any limit or deductible is applied | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, always positive, rounded half to even at the cent; held in US dollars whatever currency the loss was suffered in, never left empty |

The eleven benefits the `claim_type` parameter accepts are `trip_cancellation`, where the journey was given up before it began; `trip_interruption`, where the journey was cut short once it had begun; `medical_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency medical treatment away from home; `dental_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency dental treatment away from home; `evacuation`, where the traveller had to be moved to care or repatriated; `baggage_delay`, where the traveller's baggage arrived late and essentials had to be bought; `baggage_loss`, where the traveller's baggage or an article in it was lost or damaged; `travel_delay`, where a booked departure ran late and the traveller was out of pocket; `missed_connection`, where a late arrival caused an onward booked service to be missed; `rental_damage`, where a hired vehicle was damaged while the traveller held it; and `cancel_for_any_reason`, where the journey was given up for a reason the listed causes do not name, on a plan carrying that benefit.

## What the call returns

The call returns a single confirmation sentence naming the reference number of the claim record opened, which is a text reference beginning ccf_, the reference number of the certificate it was opened on, the claim reference the insurer quoted and the amount claimed in US dollars to two decimal places. The presence of the new claim reference in that sentence is what indicates the claim was filed; there is no other success flag.
